executive_summary: Monday opens under the shadow of dual headwinds: a ninth night of US-Iran military strikes has pushed Brent crude above $90 per barrel and reignited inflation fears, while the semiconductor sector's slide into bear market territory continues to weigh on tech sentiment. The week ahead is pivotal, with 454 companies reporting earnings including Alphabet and Tesla (Wednesday), Intel and Lockheed Martin (Thursday). The Fed holds steady at 3.50-3.75% ahead of its July 28-29 meeting, but markets increasingly price a September hike at 53% probability as oil-driven inflation pressures build. The dominant trade: rotate from beaten-down semis into defense and energy names that benefit directly from the Iran conflict, while watching GOOGL earnings as the swing factor for broader tech.

macro_events.title: US-Iran Ninth Night of Strikes — Brent Breaches $90
macro_events.causal_chain: US completes 9th consecutive night of strikes on Iranian targets → 3 US service members killed, Iran retaliates targeting US bases in Kuwait → Strait of Hormuz chokepoint risk (21% global oil + 20% LNG transits) → war-risk insurance premiums spike on VLCCs → Brent/WTI spread widens → Asian refiners begin rerouting via Cape of Good Hope (+12-14 days, +$2M per voyage) → Qatar LNG shipments to Europe at risk → Treasury revokes 60-day sanctions waiver effective July 17 → Iranian crude supply completely cut → Brent breaches $90, WTI at $84.38 → feeds into CPI via transportation and manufacturing costs → strengthens case for September Fed hike
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East, Gulf States, Asia (refiner impact), Europe (LNG supply), US (inflation transmission)
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq attack — Brent +15% in 24h, tanker stocks ran 20-35% in one week. Current conflict is sustained (9 nights) not one-off, suggesting prolonged premium.
macro_events.counterargument: SPR release could cap oil upside; diplomatic breakthrough remains possible before Trump's threatened infrastructure targeting next week. June CPI showed energy can reverse quickly (-5.7% MoM).

macro_events.title: Semiconductor Bear Market — SMH Down 20% from June Peak
macro_events.causal_chain: Samsung reports record Q2 profit (+1,800% YoY) but stock falls 8% → sell-the-news after 150% share-price run → contagion spreads: INTC -9%, AMD -6%, AMAT -6%, Micron -5% → SK Hynix delays HBM4 memory expansion in favor of DDR5 → market interprets as moderating AI memory demand growth → Chinese startup Moonshot AI narrows model gap with US leaders → questions about sustainable capex ROI → SMH enters official bear territory (-20% from late June record) → Meta-Anthropic $10B compute deal provides partial floor but insufficient → rotation from hardware to software/services
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US, South Korea, Japan, Taiwan — global semiconductor supply chain
macro_events.historical_analog: Jan 2022 chip selloff — SMH fell 35% over 9 months as rate hikes crushed growth multiples. Current drawdown at -20% may have further to run.
macro_events.counterargument: GOOGL Cloud revenue expected +67% YoY Wednesday could reaffirm AI infrastructure demand. Meta-Anthropic $10B deal proves hyperscaler spending is real. Samsung's actual results were record-breaking — valuation reset, not fundamental deterioration.

macro_events.title: Fed Holds at 3.50-3.75% — September Hike Probability Rises to 53%
macro_events.causal_chain: June CPI at 3.5% YoY — headline still elevated despite core at 2.6% → June energy prices fell 5.7% MoM but oil surge to $90 threatens reversal → Trump declares Iran ceasefire over → oil supply shock feeds into transportation, manufacturing, consumer costs → market prices 53% September hike probability (up from 47%) → 10Y yield holds 4.55%, 2Y at 4.18% → dollar DXY rebounds to 100.73 → rate-sensitive sectors (REITs, utilities, small caps) under pressure → credit spreads could widen if hiking cycle extends
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US domestic, dollar-linked emerging markets (INR, TRY, IDR weakened by strong dollar + oil import costs)
macro_events.historical_analog: 2022 rate hike cycle — energy-driven inflation forced aggressive 75bp hikes. Current environment less extreme but directionally similar.
macro_events.counterargument: Core CPI at 2.6% is within striking distance of 2% target. Fed may look through oil shock as supply-driven and transitory. July 28-29 meeting widely expected to hold.

affected_tickers.reason: Long-duration bonds lose value as rate hike expectations rise

macro_events.title: China Record $125.6B Trade Surplus — Section 122 Tariffs Expire July 24
macro_events.causal_chain: China exports surge 27% YoY in June → $125.6B surplus (2nd largest ever) → AI chip/hardware demand drives shipments → manufacturers front-load US-bound goods ahead of Section 122 expiry July 24 → 10% flat surcharge expires by statute → USTR preparing Section 301 replacement at 10-12.5% on 46+ countries → effective China tariff at 23.4% → Trump claims China election interference → trade truce jeopardized → shipping bottlenecks worsen amid Middle East war → container rates elevated → IMF cuts global growth to 3.0%, raises inflation forecast to 4.7%
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US-China bilateral, global supply chains, ASEAN rerouting countries
macro_events.historical_analog: May 2019 tariff escalation — S&P 500 fell 6% in one month as uncertainty spiked.
macro_events.counterargument: Section 301 replacement likely similar magnitude to Section 122. Front-loading already captured in June data — July shipments may normalize. Truce fundamentals remain intact for now.
